TECH-01:
Fetch /robots.txt once per scan and parse it with Protego. For each of the five AI crawlers (GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Googlebot) evaluate the Allow/Disallow rules for path "/", falling back to the wildcard group when no bot-specific group exists.
Score = allowed bots / bots with a definite ALLOWED-or-BLOCKED decision x 100.
UNKNOWN if robots.txt cannot be fetched, or if it is non-empty but fails to parse.
TECH-02:
Fetch the homepage once with a normal browser user-agent to establish a baseline response size, then fetch it again once per AI-crawler user-agent. A bot counts as blocked if it receives HTTP 403, 406 or 429, or if its response body is under 20% of the baseline size (content starvation) while the baseline itself exceeded 500 bytes.
Score = (5 - blocked bots) / 5 x 100.   Confidence 0.6.
TECH-03:
Fetch /llms.txt. Missing or empty gives 0. Otherwise: 40 base, +20 if the file holds more than 40 characters of content, +20 x the share of its web links that resolve to a working URL (or a flat +10 if the file contains no web links at all); mailto:, tel:, javascript: and #anchor links are not web links and are skipped, +20 if a date appears anywhere in it.
Score capped at 100.
TECH-04:
Scan the raw homepage HTML for overlay markers (cookie, consent, gdpr, onetrust, cookiebot, trustarc, cookieyes, modal, overlay, paywall) and for a login form or password input.
Score = 100 if neither is present; 70 if either is present but at least 150 words still survive; 20 otherwise.
Confidence 0.55.
TECH-05:
Read the XML sitemap(s) discovered from robots.txt and the well-known locations. Check every sitemap URL to test whether it resolves, and compare the set of crawled pages against the set of sitemap URLs.
Validity = resolving sitemap URLs / sitemap URLs checked x 100.
Coverage = readable crawled pages that appear in the sitemap / readable crawled pages x 100 (pages whose fetch failed or that were bot challenges are not counted).
Score = 25 + Validity x 0.45 + Coverage x 0.30 (at most 100). Requests stop at the check's 90-second time limit; the score is then from the URLs checked by then, taken evenly across the sitemap.
Score 0 if no sitemap URLs were found at all.
TECH-06:
Check every internal link found in the crawl: links to crawled pages use the crawl's own result, and links to pages the crawl did not open are fetched (up to the re-check limit, LINK_RECHECK_LIMIT, 300 by default). A link is broken if the fetch fails or returns a non-2xx status; it is a redirect chain if it takes 3 or more hops.
Score = (checked - broken) / checked x 100 - min(20, chains x 5), floored at 0. Links not checked by the check's 90-second time limit are left out.
UNKNOWN when there is no internal link to check.
Confidence 0.7.
TECH-07:
Source, in order:
  1. Field: Chrome UX Report API, origin record (phone first, then all devices) -- 75th percentile LCP, INP and CLS over the last 28 days.  Confidence 0.9.
  2. Lab (no CrUX record or no key): up to 3 key pages, in order: the homepage, then one service, article, case-study and about page, loaded one at a time in headless Chromium throttled like Lighthouse mobile (4x CPU, slow 4G). LCP, CLS and Total Blocking Time (INP's lab stand-in) per page; the median page per metric.  Confidence 0.7.  Skipped for scans of a saved site copy.
  3. Proxy (neither available): mean response latency and HTML weight of the crawled pages -- Latency <=800ms 100, <=1800ms 70, <=3000ms 40, else 20; Weight <=300KB 100, <=800KB 70, <=1.5MB 40, else 20; Score = Latency x 0.6 + Weight x 0.4.  Confidence 0.4.
Per metric (field or lab), with Google's thresholds good / poor: LCP 2.5s / 4s, INP 200ms / 500ms, TBT 200ms / 600ms, CLS 0.1 / 0.25.
   at or under good -> 100;  between -> 90 falling linearly to 50;  at or over poor -> 25.
Score = mean of the three metric scores, averaged before rounding.
TECH-08:
Score = 50 if the homepage final URL is https, + 50 if a viewport meta tag containing "width" is present.
Capped at 80 if the homepage HTML declares a fixed layout width of 1000px or more as a CSS rule (e.g. "min-width: 1200px"), which forces horizontal scrolling on a phone. Media-query breakpoints such as "@media (min-width: 1200px)" are responsive and are not counted, and neither are the rules inside a min-width media block of 768px or more, which never apply on a phone.
TECH-09:
Compare each page's raw HTML (what a crawler that does not run JavaScript reads) with a browser-rendered copy.
The crawl first renders the homepage as a probe. Per compared page: JS-only share = words that appear only after JavaScript / rendered words.
   Probe gain under the render threshold (decision "not_needed"): the site does not need rendering, and the probe is the one compared page.
   Otherwise: every page the crawl rendered is compared, and the homepage probe is always included as a row, so pages picked because they looked like empty shells do not decide the score alone.
Score = (1 - mean JS-only share across compared pages) x 100, averaged before rounding.
UNKNOWN when no rendered copy exists to compare against.
TECH-10:
Per readable page, start at 100 (a page with no headings at all is scored as having no H1). Subtract 40 if there is no H1, or 25 if there is more than one. Subtract min(30, skips x 10), where a skip is a jump of more than one heading level between consecutive headings. Floor each page at 0.
Score = mean of per-page scores.
Score 0 outright if no headings were found on any page.
TECH-11:
Heuristic baseline per page: start at 100, -30 if mean words per heading exceeds 220, -20 if heading density is under 1.5 per 1000 words, or a flat 30 if the page has no H1-H3 at all.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): up to 40 real (heading, word count of the text under that heading up to the next heading) pairs go to the model, which returns how many of those sections an assistant could lift whole.
Score = liftable sections / sections sent x 100, the model's count clamped to 0..sections sent; a reply with no usable count leaves the heuristic score.
0 (Fail) when no page has enough body text to judge.
TECH-12:
Count <table> elements and <ul>/<ol> elements across every crawled page.
Only tables and lists in page content count; navigation, header, footer and sidebar lists are excluded.
Score = 100 if tables + lists >= 8; 70 if >= 3; else 40.
TECH-13:
Per page:
   Text-to-code = visible text characters / total HTML characters x 100, then banded, because a byte ratio is not a score (a content-rich page sits near 20-25% and never approaches 100):
      >=25% -> 100,  >=15% -> 85,  >=10% -> 70,  >=5% -> 45,  else 20
Score = mean of each page's banded ratio across the readable crawled pages.
When a page's text was read from a browser-rendered copy, the rendered HTML is the denominator, so text and markup come from the same document.
Content depth (word count) is not part of this check: it is ON-10's measure, and scoring it here as well charged a thin page twice.
TECH-14: Collect every across the crawl. Alt text counts as usable if it is non-empty, longer than 3 characters, and not one of the placeholder values image/img/logo. Count videos --
TECH-15:
A page counts as dated if it exposes a published or modified date through article:published_time, article:modified_time or a <time> element, or through datePublished/dateModified in its JSON-LD.
Score = 60 + (dated pages / pages) x 40.
The 60 floor is deliberate: dates matter most on articles, so their absence on home and service pages is treated as partial rather than a total failure.
TECH-16:
Find the site's Organization in the homepage JSON-LD, merging every Organization node that shares the first one's @id or name, including nested ones such as a Service provider or Article publisher. Expected fields are name, url, logo and sameAs; address/location and contactPoint/email/telephone count as a bonus group.
Score = (expected fields present / 4) x 80 + 20 if any address or contact field is present.
Score 0 if no Organization node exists.
TECH-17:
Map each page detected type to the schema.org types that genuinely satisfy it, matched by exact type name (an OfferCatalog is not an Offer):
   article     -> Article, BlogPosting, NewsArticle, TechArticle, Report
   service     -> Service, Product, Offer, ProfessionalService and their subtypes (FinancialService, LegalService, GovernmentService, ProductModel, ProductGroup, IndividualProduct, SomeProducts, AggregateOffer)
   about       -> Organization, Corporation, LocalBusiness, NGO and the other Organization subtypes, AboutPage
   home        -> the same organization types, WebSite
   case_study  -> Article, CaseStudy, CreativeWork
Pages of other types are not counted.
Score = matched pages / applicable pages x 100; 0 (Fail) if no page is applicable. The types expected on key (service or product) pages come from the industry profile: Product for a manufacturer, SoftwareApplication for software, MedicalWebPage for healthcare.
TECH-18:
Collect author markup across the crawl: Person nodes, and people named in the author field of JSON-LD.
Not counted: an author that is an Organization, and visible bylines ([rel=author], .author, .byline), which are not machine-readable markup and are judged by ON-12.
Score = 0 (Fail) with no author markup; 80 when any is found; 95 when any author carries a jobTitle.
Confidence 0.65.
TECH-19:
Count every JSON-LD block found across the crawl and how many parsed successfully.
Score = valid blocks / total blocks x 100.
Every block is named by its @type -- a broken block's type is read from its raw text -- and each broken block gives its reason in plain words (for example a raw line break inside a text value). The recommendation names the broken blocks and their pages.
N/A when the site has no JSON-LD at all: there is nothing to validate, and whether markup should exist is already scored by TECH-16 (Organization), TECH-17 (page type) and TECH-18 (author).
With fewer than 3 blocks on the whole site the result is flagged as resting on very little markup, at confidence 0.4.
TECH-20:
Per page, flag a problem when: no canonical link is present; or an absolute canonical points to a path that differs from the page own final path (the homepage page itself excepted; a non-home page canonicalised to the homepage IS a problem); or the page took 3 or more redirect hops.
Score = pages with no problem / pages x 100.
TECH-21:
Applies only to a multi-country site. The site's countries and languages are read from: country locale prefixes (/en-us/, /de-de/) that each open at least three URLs, which give both the country and the language; page paths that exist under two language prefixes (at least three, /en/about and /fr/about); the languages and regions pages declare in <html lang> (en-US, en-GB); and the site's own hreflang tags (x-default ignored). URLs are read from the crawled pages, their links and the sitemap; a two-letter site section (/dc/, /go/) on its own is not a market.
One country and one language = N/A, whether or not some hreflang tags exist: there are no country or language versions for hreflang to link, so the check is left out of the score.
Two or more countries or languages and no hreflang = 0 (Fail).
Two or more countries or languages with hreflang: a tag is valid if it carries both a lang and an href. Score = valid tags / tags x 100.
TECH-22:
Across every readable crawled page (failed fetches and bot challenges excluded), measure four things:
   Presence               = pages with both a title and a meta description / pages
   Title uniqueness       = distinct non-empty titles / non-empty titles
   Description uniqueness = distinct non-empty descriptions / non-empty descriptions
   Length quality         = pages with a 20-70 char title AND a 70-170 char description / pages
Score = Presence x 50 + Title uniqueness x 15 + Description uniqueness x 10 + Length quality x 25.
ON-01:
Eligible headings are H1-H3 on service, home and case-study pages (pages whose URL path contains "service" included; every page when the site has none of these) that have at least 3 words and are not a bare navigation label (home, about, services, blog, pricing ...).
Heuristic baseline: a heading counts as a question if it opens with how/what/why/when/where/which/who/can/should/is/are/do/does/will or ends with a question mark.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): every distinct eligible heading goes to the model once (a heading repeated across pages is judged once and weighted by how often it appears), which decides which are questions a BUYER would actually ask.
Question share = buyer questions / headings assessed, then banded:
   >=33% -> 100,  >=20% -> 85,  >=10% -> 65,  >=3% -> 45,  else 25
0 (Fail) if the site has no eligible headings at all.
ON-02:
For every question-phrased H1-H3, take the text between it and the next heading as the answer.
   Base    = 70 if the answer runs to 20 words or more, else 30
   Bonus   = +30 if the answer is 40-60 words (the target window), or +15 if it is 25-90 words
   Per-answer score capped at 100
Score = mean across all answers.
0 (Fail), with the reason, when the site has no question headings.
ON-03:
Derive the core concepts from the site own navigation and service-page titles (never a fixed keyword list - every audited site is a different business).
Heuristic baseline: for each concept, look at a 200-character window around its first mention and test for a definition pattern (concept + is/are/means/refers to/helps).
LLM pass (authoritative when available): the model receives each (concept, surrounding window) pair and decides whether the text gives a clear, complete definition rather than a passing mention.
Score = concepts defined / concepts assessed x 100.   0 (Fail) if none of the site's core concepts appears in its text.
ON-04:
Take the opening (first two substantial sentences, up to 400 characters) of every page.
Heuristic baseline: 85 if the opening names a site-specific term and avoids filler openings ("welcome to", "in today's", "we are a leading"), 55 if it names a term but also opens with filler, 35 otherwise.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): the model judges per opening whether it leads with a specific, concrete statement rather than boilerplate.
Score = openings leading with substance / openings assessed x 100.
Pages with no opening paragraph are left out of the average; 0 (Fail) if no page has one.
ON-05:
Identify service and solution pages (page type service, or a URL path containing service/solution). A page satisfies the check if it has a heading matching FAQ / frequently asked, or carries FAQPage schema.
Score = qualifying pages / service pages x 100.
UNKNOWN when the site has no service or solution pages, since there is nothing the check applies to.
The homepage counts only when the site has no service or solution pages of its own.
ON-06:
Consider pages that carry FAQPage JSON-LD or show an FAQ heading (FAQ / Frequently asked).
Per page: 50 if the FAQPage markup is valid (Question entries with a name and an accepted answer) + 50 if every marked-up question also appears in the page text. A visible FAQ with no markup earns 0: this check is about the schema, and ON-05 credits the visible FAQ.
Score = mean across those pages. 0 (Fail) when no page has FAQ markup, whether or not FAQs are visible.
ON-07:
Heuristic baseline: a page shows evaluation intent if its title, opening text or URL path contains a word starting vs / versus / compar / alternative / pricing / feature / capabilit, or it is a service page.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): every page with text goes to the model, which decides which are pages where a buyer is actively evaluating or comparing options. The numerator stays the measured fact - does that page carry a real HTML <table>.
Score = evaluation pages with a table / evaluation pages x 100.   0 (Fail) if none qualify.
ON-08:
Collect content lists - <ul>/<ol> with 2 or more items that are not inside <nav>, <header> or <footer>, so repeated menus are excluded.
Heuristic baseline: a list is useful if it has 3 or more items and mentions step/how/benefit/includ/deliver/process.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): every content list goes to the model, which judges whether each is genuinely useful for answering a question rather than decorative filler.
Score = useful lists / lists assessed x 100.   Score 35 if no content lists exist.
ON-09:
Peak single CONTENT-word density per page (function words removed), averaged across pages, banded:
   <3.5% -> 100,  <6% -> 75,  else 45
UNKNOWN if no page has at least 40 content words.
ON-10:
The rubric is 8 points a complete service page should cover: problem/need, approach or methodology, what is included, outcomes or benefits, who it is for, pricing or commercial model, proof, and a clear next step.
Heuristic baseline: keyword presence per rubric point.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): an excerpt of every key page goes to the model, which counts how many checklist points each page ACTUALLY covers. The denominator is unchanged - the same pages, out of the same checklist.
Score = mean(points covered / checklist points) x 100, with each page's count clamped to 0..checklist points; a reply with no readable count is left out.
The checklist comes from the site's industry profile (industry_profiles.json): specifications, standards and datasheets for a manufacturer; engagement model and named clients for an IT-services firm; the eight general points above otherwise.
ON-11:
Major pages are home, service, case-study and about pages (not every blog post).
A statistic is a percentage, an N+ figure, a currency amount, a multiplier (3x), a thousands-separated number, or a scaled figure (2.5 million). Bare four-digit years are explicitly excluded.
Heuristic baseline: Score = major pages carrying at least one statistic / major pages x 100.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): every major page that carries a statistic goes to the model with their figures and an excerpt, and it decides whether at least one of them is ORIGINAL to this company rather than quoted off a third party.
Score = (major pages with a statistic / major pages) x (pages judged original / pages assessed) x 100, so the denominator stays every major page and only the numerator moves.
ON-12:
Collect visible [rel=author], .author or .byline elements and the authors named in JSON-LD across the crawl, capturing the byline TEXT rather than only the fact that an element matched. An element with no text is not a signal, and each person is counted once per page (markup and a visible byline naming the same person are one byline).
Heuristic baseline: Score = 80 if any author signal exists anywhere, else 30.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): every byline goes to the model, which decides for each whether it names a specific real person - not a company, and not a generic label such as "Admin" or "Editorial Team" - and whether it states that person's role or credentials.
Score = named people / assessed x 50 + named people who also state a role / assessed x 50, floored at 30: markup that names nobody is no worse than no markup at all.
ON-13:
Heuristic baseline, per page: 25 if the copy mentions a client/customer/partner, + 30 if it contains a quantified figure, + 25 if it describes deployment (deploy/implementation/production/rolled out), + 20 bonus when both a client mention and a figure are present. Score = mean across pages.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): every page with text goes to the model, which judges the same three signals by reading them - does the page NAME a specific client organisation, is the outcome genuinely quantified, is deployment actually described.
Score = mean of the same 25/30/25/+20 rubric applied to the model's verdicts, so the rubric is unchanged and only the reading of each signal improves.
ON-14:
A claim is a sentence of more than 6 words containing a statistic (same pattern as ON-11, years excluded). Each distinct sentence is one claim, however many pages repeat it.
Heuristic baseline: a claim counts as sourced if the sentence contains, as whole words, the anchor text (4+ characters) of a link on that page, or the words source / according to / report. Score = sourced claims / claims x 100.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): every claim goes to the model together with any adjacent link anchor text, and it decides whether each is attributed to a source a reader could actually check - a named organisation, publication, study or dated report.
Score = attributed claims / claims assessed x 100.   0 (Fail) if no claims were found.
ON-15:
Score = 50 + (pages exposing a published or modified date / pages) x 50.
Confidence 0.6.
ON-16:
The six buyer-journey stages are awareness, qualification, comparison, objection, trust and decision.
Heuristic baseline: keyword matching (each keyword must start a word) over each page title, opening text and URL path.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): the titles and URLs of every page go to the model, which decides which of the six stages the site has content for.
Score = stages covered / 6 x 100.
ON-17:
Heuristic baseline: match each page URL path and title against best ... for / vs / versus / alternative, as whole words.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): the titles and URLs of every page go to the model, which decides which are genuinely built to answer a high-intent comparison query rather than merely containing the words.
Score = 80 if 3 or more such pages are found; 45 if at least one; else 15.
ON-18:
Compare page titles as token sets (4+ character tokens) using Jaccard similarity. Two pages are CANDIDATES to compete when similarity >= 0.7 and the titles are not identical strings (exactly duplicated titles are TECH-22's title-uniqueness measure, so they are not charged twice).
Comparison uses an exact prefix filter, not all pairs, so the result is identical to comparing every pair but runs in seconds at the 2500-page crawl ceiling.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): every candidate pair goes to the model, which confirms which of them really answer the same buyer question. Unconfirmed pairs stop counting against the site; candidates past the sample keep their heuristic verdict rather than being silently dropped.
Clean share = 1 - (pages in a competing pair / pages compared), then banded:
   100% -> 100,  >=95% -> 90,  >=85% -> 75,  >=70% -> 60,  else 40
UNKNOWN if no page has a title; 0 (Fail) with only one title.
ON-19:
Thin pages are non-utility pages under 180 words. Near-duplicates are pages whose first 400 characters overlap at Jaccard >= 0.72, found with the same exact prefix filter as ON-18.
Clean share = 1 - (pages that are thin or duplicated / pages assessed), then banded:
   >=95% -> 100,  >=85% -> 85,  >=70% -> 70,  >=50% -> 55,  else 40
UNKNOWN if there are no content pages.
ON-20:
Derive the site own category terms from its navigation and service-page titles, and its geographies from its structured data and address text, plus a generic reach list (global, worldwide, United States, Europe ...).
A page qualifies when its copy or title names a brand term AND a category term AND a geography term, each as whole words ("usa" is not found in "thousand"). The page URL is not read: it always contains the site's own host, which is one of the brand terms.
Score = qualifying pages / pages x 100.   Confidence 0.7.
0 (Fail) when the site's own categories or brand name cannot be derived.
OFF-01:
Search Wikidata (wbsearchentities) and Wikipedia (search API) for the company name. When the Company Identity Agent has already confirmed the company's Wikidata item or Wikipedia article for this scan, that confirmed record decides the presence instead of a name search. No model is asked.
On Wikidata = a search result whose label contains the company's whole name with its legal form removed ("Evoke Technologies", not just "Evoke": Evoke plc is another company). On Wikipedia = a search result whose title contains the company's whole name in the same way.
Score = 100 when the company is on both, 0 when either is missing.
UNKNOWN only when a source that could still decide the result is unreachable (one confirmed absence already gives 0).
Name fallback: when a search for the full company name returns nothing, it is repeated with the trailing legal form removed (plc, Inc, Ltd, LLC, Corp, GmbH, Private Limited ...), since directories list the trading name, and then once more without a trailing abbreviation of the name ("... Surgeons AAOS"), each only when it gives a different name. A failed search is not retried.
OFF-02:
Search Wikidata for the company name (the same lookup as OFF-01, made once per scan). Take the first entity whose label contains the company's whole name with its legal form removed (as OFF-01).
Score = 0 when no entity names the company: there is no record for a Knowledge Panel to be built from.
Otherwise score = 50 + 30 if the entity has a description + 20 if the brand term is in its label (max 100). Because the entity is chosen by its label naming the company, the +20 is met by nearly every entity found, so in practice the scores are 0, 70 or 100.
UNKNOWN only when Wikidata is unreachable.
Name fallback: when a search for the full company name returns nothing, it is repeated with the trailing legal form removed (plc, Inc, Ltd, LLC, Corp, GmbH, Private Limited ...), since directories list the trading name, and then once more without a trailing abbreviation of the name ("... Surgeons AAOS"), each only when it gives a different name. A failed search is not retried.
OFF-03:
One web search (Google Custom Search API, or OpenAI web search when Google is not configured): "<company name>" (site:<each profile site checked>); by default site:linkedin.com OR site:crunchbase.com OR site:bloomberg.com OR site:zoominfo.com. A platform is found when at least one result link is on it.
The sites checked come from the industry profile chosen or detected for the scan (industry_profiles.json; it replaces the default set), plus the sites of the region chosen (offpage_platforms.json). The query names every site checked.
Presence = min(platforms found, N) / N x 70, where N = 4 (scoring_rules.json platforms_for_full_marks) or the number of sites checked if fewer; with the default four sites this is platforms found / 4 x 70.
Name consistency = share of found platforms whose result titles/snippets contain the company name or brand term.
Location consistency = share of found platforms whose result titles/snippets mention, as whole words, one of the office locations the site itself states (from its structured data and address text). Two-letter codes (US, IN, PA) are not used: they match ordinary words such as "us" and "in". Name matching is whole-word too.
Score = presence + name consistency x 15 + location consistency x 15.
UNKNOWN when the web search fails (not configured, quota used up or unreachable).
Name fallback: when a search for the full company name returns nothing, it is repeated with the trailing legal form removed (plc, Inc, Ltd, LLC, Corp, GmbH, Private Limited ...), since directories list the trading name, and then once more without a trailing abbreviation of the name ("... Surgeons AAOS"), each only when it gives a different name. A failed search is not retried.
If the site states no office location, the company-name match carries all 30 consistency points. The sites checked come from the industry profile (for a manufacturer: LinkedIn, ZoomInfo, Crunchbase, Bloomberg, Thomasnet, GlobalSpec and Kompass).
N/A when the industry profile lists no business-profile sites (for example review sites for a manufacturer): the channel does not apply, so the check is left out of the score rather than failed.
OFF-04:
Scan the text of every crawled page for certification claims: certified/accredited, compliance/compliant, licensed, an ISO standard number (ISO 9001, ISO 27001 ...), CMMI, and partner tiers (certified/authorized/accredited/premier/gold/platinum/elite partner).
Score = 55 when at least one kind of claim is found, 40 when none is.
Capped at 55: issuer registries are not queried, so the claims are unverified.
Evidence only, no effect on the score: one web search off the company's own site for the specific certificates it names (ISO numbers, CMMI, partner tiers); up to three result pages are opened to confirm they name the company and the certificate, and the outcome is recorded as verification_result.
Name fallback: when a search for the full company name returns nothing, it is repeated with the trailing legal form removed (plc, Inc, Ltd, LLC, Corp, GmbH, Private Limited ...), since directories list the trading name, and then once more without a trailing abbreviation of the name ("... Surgeons AAOS"), each only when it gives a different name. A failed search is not retried.
N/A for a clearly non-IT industry (healthcare, manufacturing, retail, finance, as detected or chosen for the audit): CMMI, ISO and technology-partner tiers are IT-services credentials. An unclear industry (General) is still scored.
OFF-05:
One web search (Google Custom Search API, or OpenAI web search when Google is not configured): "<company name>" (site:<each review site checked>); by default site:g2.com OR site:clutch.co OR site:gartner.com OR site:trustradius.com. A platform is found when at least one result link is on it.
The sites checked come from the industry profile chosen or detected for the scan (industry_profiles.json; it replaces the default set), plus the sites of the region chosen (offpage_platforms.json). The query names every site checked.
Presence = min(platforms found, N) / N x 70, where N = 4 (scoring_rules.json platforms_for_full_marks) or the number of sites checked if fewer; with the default four sites this is platforms found / 4 x 70.
Category placement: the site's own categories are derived from its navigation and service pages. Heuristic baseline: a match when a category term appears in the found listings' titles/snippets. LLM pass (authoritative when available): the model decides whether the listings place the company in the same or a clearly equivalent category.
Score = presence + 30 if the category matches (0 if not, or if no listing was found); if no category can be derived from the site, presence carries the whole score (platforms found / N x 100). Sites checked come from the industry profile.
UNKNOWN when the web search fails.
Name fallback: when a search for the full company name returns nothing, it is repeated with the trailing legal form removed (plc, Inc, Ltd, LLC, Corp, GmbH, Private Limited ...), since directories list the trading name, and then once more without a trailing abbreviation of the name ("... Surgeons AAOS"), each only when it gives a different name. A failed search is not retried.
N/A when the industry profile lists no review sites (for example review sites for a manufacturer): the channel does not apply, so the check is left out of the score rather than failed.
OFF-06:
The sites checked come from the industry profile chosen or detected for the scan (industry_profiles.json; it replaces the default set), plus the sites of the region chosen (offpage_platforms.json). One web search (Google Custom Search API, or OpenAI web search when Google is not configured): "<company name>" reviews (site:<each review site checked>); by default site:g2.com OR site:clutch.co OR site:gartner.com OR site:trustradius.com. Review results = result links on the review sites checked.
Volume = min(60, review results x 12).
Recency: each result's date is the date its page publishes (article/og metadata) or the date the search result shows. Newest dated result within 365 days = 40; within 730 days = 20; older or no date = 0. A date that is not a real calendar date, or is in the future, is ignored.
Score = volume + recency.
UNKNOWN when the web search fails. Review counts inside each platform are not read.

Topic = Wikidata's short description of the confirmed company (4 words or fewer) when there is one, otherwise the site's main category, derived from its navigation and service pages.
Search 1: best <topic> companies ("companies" is left off when the topic already ends in a noun such as organization, association or firm). If the brand term appears as whole words in any result's title, snippet or address, score = 100.
Otherwise search 2: "<company name>" (best OR top OR leading) <topic>. List pages = results whose title contains best, top or leading and that are not on the company's own site.
Score = 60 at 2 or more list pages, 40 at 1, 10 with none.
